old.desc:
Beyond Nigeria — Preparing for Anglophone West Africa
PassEscort is not staying in Nigeria. I want you thinking, from now, like someone preparing to sell across Ghana, Sierra Leone, Liberia, and The Gambia — not as an afterthought, but as the plan.
This Week's Focus:
Understanding what is shared across Anglophone West African markets (English-language exams, mobile-first behaviour, price-conscious households) and what will differ (currency, exam boards like WASSCE variants, telco partners, local trust networks).
Daily Practice:
Research, country by country, the equivalent of WAEC/JAMB in Ghana, Sierra Leone, Liberia, and The Gambia — write one paragraph per country on how students there prepare for their exams today.
Identify one telecom provider or mobile money platform per country that could be a future distribution partner, and note why.
Draft how your Nigerian pitch from Week 7 would need to change for a Ghanaian parent, in tone and example, even before it changes in substance.
Watch This Week:
Anthony Iannarino — for B2B fundamentals that travel well across any market, once adapted.
Note: there is no single YouTube channel built specifically for West African market entry — this is a gap you will need to fill with direct research this week, not video-watching alone. Use local news sites and each country's exam board website as your primary sources.
Reflect:
Which of the four markets do you believe PassEscort should enter second, after Nigeria, and why?

old.desc:
— Negotiation & the Art of Closing
Closing is not pressuring someone into a decision. It is removing the real, honest obstacles between where they are and the decision they already want to make.
This Week's Focus:
Tactical negotiation, objection handling, and closing with integrity — never manipulation.
Daily Practice:
Take the five objections from your Sales Playbook's objection-handling table and practice responding to each out loud, from memory, until it is natural.
Practice 'labelling' emotions in a conversation — saying things like 'it sounds like cost is the real concern here' — and notice how it opens people up rather than closing them off.
Watch This Week:
Chris Voss / The Black Swan Group — for tactical empathy and negotiation — his FBI hostage-negotiation background translates directly into sales conversations.
Dan Lok — for tonality, confidence, and closing high-value conversations without sounding desperate.
Reflect:
Recall a real disagreement you navigated well in your own life. What did you do there that you can bring into a sales negotiation?



 — Winning the Nigerian Market
A script written for an American SaaS buyer will not work, word for word, on a Nigerian parent standing at a school gate. This week is about translating everything you've learned into our own context.

This Week's Focus:
Understanding Nigerian buyer psychology — price sensitivity, trust built through community and referral, the role of parents versus students in the decision, and the power of word-of-mouth over advertising.

Daily Practice:
Interview 3 parents specifically about how they decide to spend money on their children's education — what convinces them, what makes them suspicious.
Rewrite your Week 5 and 6 scripts in a way that would feel natural to a parent in Nigeria, not a script translated from an American YouTube video.

Watch This Week:
Dayo Adetiloye Business Hub — for grounded, practical Nigerian entrepreneurship and market insight.

Victor Antonio — for scenario-based sales breakdowns you can adapt to our own market conversations.

Reflect:
What is one thing that builds trust with a Nigerian parent that would never appear in an international sales course?

card.desc:
Cold Calling & Prospecting Mastery
This is where preparation meets the real world. Cold outreach is uncomfortable for everyone at the start — the difference between an amateur and a professional is that the professional does it anyway, and does it daily.

This Week's Focus:
Building the courage and the craft to reach out to people who don't yet know you, confidently and without sounding like a script.

Daily Practice:
Make 10 practice cold approaches a day — to family friends, market contacts, anyone willing — purely for practice, not yet for conversion.

Record yourself on your phone during at least 3 of these calls this week, and listen back. This will feel uncomfortable. Do it anyway.

Watch This Week:
Art Sobczak (Smart Calling) — for practical, non-pushy cold calling technique.

Becc Holland / Flip the Script — for modern, creative prospecting that doesn't feel like an old-fashioned sales call.

Sales Gravy (Jeb Blount) — for the mindset of 'fanatical prospecting' — the discipline of never letting the pipeline run dry.

Reflect:
What is the exact moment in a cold call where your confidence tends to drop — and what will you do differently next time?

WEEK 3 — Sales Psychology I — Trust, Rapport & Influence
People buy from those they trust, long before they buy what is being offered. This week begins your real education in the psychology behind every 'yes.'

1. Daily Practice:
Practice mirroring tone and pace in ordinary conversations this week — with family, with market sellers, with anyone — and notice how it changes the warmth of the exchange.

2. Read (or find summarised online) Robert Cialdini's six principles of influence — reciprocity, commitment, social proof, authority, liking, and scarcity — and write one PassEscort example for each.

3. Watch This Week:
Vanessa Van Edwards (Science of People) — for body language, charisma, and building rapport quickly and genuinely.
Jill Konrath — for the psychology behind buyer decision-making.

4. Reflect:
Which of Cialdini's six principles comes most naturally to you, and which will you need to deliberately practice?

5. Reflect:
What did you hear this week that surprised you about what parents or students actually want?

Sales Psychology II — The Art of the Right Question
The best closers I have studied talk less than you'd expect. They ask questions that lead the other person to convince themselves. This week, you learn that skill.

2a. This Week's Focus:
Questioning frameworks that uncover a prospect's real pain and let them arrive at their own 'yes.'

2b. Daily Practice:
Take one PassEscort conversation each day and rewrite it entirely as a sequence of questions, with almost no statements.
Practice sitting in silence after asking a meaningful question — resist the urge to fill the silence yourself.

2c. Watch This Week:
Jeremy Miner / 7th Level (YouTube: @jeremyminer) — for his NEPQ questioning method — this is one of the most important channels in this entire plan.

2d. Reflect:
Write down three questions you could ask a parent that would help them discover, on their own, why their child needs PassEscort.

cards.desc:
— Negotiation & the Art of Closing
Closing is not pressuring someone into a decision. It is removing the real, honest obstacles between where they are and the decision they already want to make.

This Week's Focus:
Tactical negotiation, objection handling, and closing with integrity — never manipulation.

Daily Practice:
Take the five objections from your Sales Playbook's objection-handling table and practice responding to each out loud, from memory, until it is natural.

Practice 'labelling' emotions in a conversation — saying things like 'it sounds like cost is the real concern here' — and notice how it opens people up rather than closing them off.

Watch This Week:
Chris Voss / The Black Swan Group — for tactical empathy and negotiation — his FBI hostage-negotiation background translates directly into sales conversations.

Dan Lok — for tonality, confidence, and closing high-value conversations without sounding desperate.

Reflect:
Recall a real disagreement you navigated well in your own life. What did you do there that you can bring into a sales negotiation?



 Winning the Nigerian Market
A script written for an American SaaS buyer will not work, word for word, on a Nigerian parent standing at a school gate. This week is about translating everything you've learned into our own context.

This Week's Focus:
Understanding Nigerian buyer psychology — price sensitivity, trust built through community and referral, the role of parents versus students in the decision, and the power of word-of-mouth over advertising.

Daily Practice:
Interview 3 parents specifically about how they decide to spend money on their children's education — what convinces them, what makes them suspicious.
Rewrite your Week 5 and 6 scripts in a way that would feel natural to a parent in Nigeria, not a script translated from an American YouTube video.

Watch This Week:
Dayo Adetiloye Business Hub — for grounded, practical Nigerian entrepreneurship and market insight.

Victor Antonio — for scenario-based sales breakdowns you can adapt to our own market conversations.

Reflect:
What is one thing that builds trust with a Nigerian parent that would never appear in an international sales course?

cards.desc:
Sales Psychology I — Trust, Rapport & Influence
People buy from those they trust, long before they buy what is being offered. This week begins your real education in the psychology behind every 'yes.'

1a. Daily Practice:
Practice mirroring tone and pace in ordinary conversations this week — with family, with market sellers, with anyone — and notice how it changes the warmth of the exchange.

1b. Read (or find summarised online) Robert Cialdini's six principles of influence — reciprocity, commitment, social proof, authority, liking, and scarcity — and write one PassEscort example for each.

1c. Watch This Week:
Vanessa Van Edwards (Science of People) — for body language, charisma, and building rapport quickly and genuinely.
Jill Konrath — for the psychology behind buyer decision-making.

1d. Reflect:
Which of Cialdini's six principles comes most naturally to you, and which will you need to deliberately practice?

1e. Reflect:
What did you hear this week that surprised you about what parents or students actually want?

Sales Psychology II — The Art of the Right Question
The best closers I have studied talk less than you'd expect. They ask questions that lead the other person to convince themselves. This week, you learn that skill.

2a. This Week's Focus:
Questioning frameworks that uncover a prospect's real pain and let them arrive at their own 'yes.'

2b. Daily Practice:
Take one PassEscort conversation each day and rewrite it entirely as a sequence of questions, with almost no statements.
Practice sitting in silence after asking a meaningful question — resist the urge to fill the silence yourself.

2c. Watch This Week:
Jeremy Miner / 7th Level (YouTube: @jeremyminer) — for his NEPQ questioning method — this is one of the most important channels in this entire plan.

2d. Reflect:
Write down three questions you could ask a parent that would help them discover, on their own, why their child needs PassEscort.
cards.name: For Roselyn

cards.desc:
Cold Calling & Prospecting Mastery
This is where preparation meets the real world. Cold outreach is uncomfortable for everyone at the start — the difference between an amateur and a professional is that the professional does it anyway, and does it daily.

This Week's Focus:
Building the courage and the craft to reach out to people who don't yet know you, confidently and without sounding like a script.

Daily Practice:
Make 10 practice cold approaches a day — to family friends, market contacts, anyone willing — purely for practice, not yet for conversion.

Record yourself on your phone during at least 3 of these calls this week, and listen back. This will feel uncomfortable. Do it anyway.

Watch This Week:
Art Sobczak (Smart Calling) — for practical, non-pushy cold calling technique.

Becc Holland / Flip the Script — for modern, creative prospecting that doesn't feel like an old-fashioned sales call.

Sales Gravy (Jeb Blount) — for the mindset of 'fanatical prospecting' — the discipline of never letting the pipeline run dry.

Reflect:
What is the exact moment in a cold call where your confidence tends to drop — and what will you do differently next time?

cards.desc:
Beyond Nigeria — Preparing for Anglophone West Africa

PassEscort is not staying in Nigeria. I want you thinking, from now, like someone preparing to sell across Ghana, Sierra Leone, Liberia, and The Gambia — not as an afterthought, but as the plan.

This Week's Focus:
Understanding what is shared across Anglophone West African markets (English-language exams, mobile-first behaviour, price-conscious households) and what will differ (currency, exam boards like WASSCE variants, telco partners, local trust networks).

Daily Practice:
Research, country by country, the equivalent of WAEC/JAMB in Ghana, Sierra Leone, Liberia, and The Gambia — write one paragraph per country on how students there prepare for their exams today.

Identify one telecom provider or mobile money platform per country that could be a future distribution partner, and note why.

Draft how your Nigerian pitch from Week 7 would need to change for a Ghanaian parent, in tone and example, even before it changes in substance.

Watch This Week:
Anthony Iannarino — for B2B fundamentals that travel well across any market, once adapted.

Note: there is no single YouTube channel built specifically for West African market entry — this is a gap you will need to fill with direct research this week, not video-watching alone. Use local news sites and each country's exam board website as your primary sources.

Reflect:
Which of the four markets do you believe PassEscort should enter second, after Nigeria, and why?
